q: Which SDLC model is most suitable when the requirements are clearly understood and fixed in advance, and each phase must be completed before the next one begins?
exp: The Waterfall model is a linear sequential model that works best for stable, well-understood requirements.

q: Which of the following is NOT a desirable characteristic of a good Software Requirements Specification (SRS)?
options: Containing detailed implementation and coding decisions
exp: An SRS should state what the system must do, not how it is implemented; embedding design/coding decisions is undesirable.

q: Which type of coupling between two modules is the most undesirable (highest degree of coupling)?
exp: Content coupling, where one module directly modifies or relies on the internals of another, is the strongest and worst form of coupling.

q: In the SOLID principles of object-oriented design, the Single Responsibility Principle says that:
options: a class should be open for extension but closed for modification
a class should have only one reason to change
subclasses must be replaceable for their base class
clients should not depend on interfaces they do not use
exp: S = Single Responsibility (one reason to change). The other options describe Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution and Interface Segregation respectively.

q: A program flow graph has 14 edges and 11 nodes and is a single connected graph. What is its cyclomatic complexity V(G)?
Which of the following activities is an example of preventive maintenance?
options: Restructuring and refactoring code to reduce future maintenance problems
Fixing a crash reported by a user
Porting the software to a new operating system
Adding a new report requested by the client
exp: Preventive maintenance improves the internal structure (e.g., refactoring) to avoid future problems; the other options are corrective, adaptive and perfective.

q: The Singleton design pattern is used to:
options: create objects without specifying their exact class
add behaviour to an object dynamically
ensure a class has only one instance with a global access point
exp: Singleton is a creational pattern restricting a class to one instance. Factory creates objects without naming the class, Decorator adds behaviour, Observer notifies dependents.

q: In the Critical Path Method (CPM) of project scheduling, the critical path is
options: The shortest path from start to end
The longest path from start to end of the activity network
The path having the largest number of activities
The path having the maximum slack
exp: The critical path is the longest duration path; it has zero slack and determines the minimum project duration.

q: In the SEI Capability Maturity Model (CMM), which maturity level is known as the 'Defined' level?
exp: CMM levels are 1 Initial, 2 Repeatable, 3 Defined, 4 Managed, 5 Optimizing.

q: Which design pattern defines a one-to-many dependency so that when one object changes state all its dependents are notified automatically?
exp: Observer is a behavioural pattern (publish-subscribe style). Singleton is creational; Adapter and Facade are structural.

q: The distinguishing feature of the Spiral model compared with other process models is
options: Explicit risk analysis in every iteration
exp: Each loop of the Spiral model includes risk identification and resolution, making it risk-driven.

q: Which of the following is a non-functional requirement?
options: The system shall calculate income tax from the salary entered
The system shall allow users to search products by name
The system shall respond to any search query within 2 seconds
The system shall generate a monthly sales report
exp: Response time is a performance constraint (quality attribute), hence non-functional; the others describe functions.

q: Which type of cohesion is the strongest (most desirable)?
exp: Functional cohesion, where all elements contribute to a single well-defined task, is the highest level of cohesion.

q: The main purpose of regression testing is to
options: Test only the newly added feature
Measure system performance under heavy load
Verify that changes have not broken previously working functionality
exp: Regression testing re-runs earlier tests after modification to catch unintended side effects.

q: A project has an Unadjusted Function Point count of 125 and the sum of the 14 general system characteristic ratings is 30. Using FP = UFP × (0.65 + 0.01 × ΣFi), the function point count is
Among the following white-box coverage criteria, which is the strongest?
exp: Path coverage requires every independent execution path to be exercised and subsumes branch coverage, which in turn subsumes statement coverage.

q: A static program analysis tool
options: Examines source code without executing it to detect potential defects
Executes the program with test data to measure statement coverage
Measures the response time of a running application under load
Automatically generates the graphical user interface
exp: Static analysis inspects code (e.g., for uninitialized variables, unreachable code) without running it.

q: Using basic COCOMO for an organic project, effort E = 2.4 × (KLOC)^1.05 person-months. For a 10 KLOC project the effort is approximately
Which ISO/IEC standard defines the software life cycle processes?
exp: ISO/IEC 12207 establishes a framework of processes for the software life cycle; the others deal with environment, security and food safety.

q: In throw-away (rapid) prototyping, the prototype is:
options: discarded after the requirements have been clarified
exp: The throw-away prototype is built to elicit and validate requirements and is then discarded; the real system is built with proper design. Evolutionary prototyping instead refines the prototype into the product.

q: In Boehm's spiral model diagram, the radial distance from the centre represents:
options: the cumulative cost incurred so far
the size of the development team
exp: In the spiral model the radial dimension is cumulative cost to date, while the angular dimension represents progress through the quadrants of each cycle.

q: Which of the following is NOT a requirements elicitation technique?
exp: Code inspection is a verification activity on source code, not a technique for gathering requirements.

q: In a data flow diagram (DeMarco/Yourdon notation), a circle (bubble) represents a
exp: A bubble denotes a process that transforms input data flows into output data flows.

q: A field accepts an integer age from 18 to 60. Which set of test values best represents boundary value analysis?
exp: BVA tests values at and immediately around each boundary: 17, 18, 19 and 59, 60, 61.

q: A project of 24 KLOC was completed in 48 person-months. The productivity in LOC per person-month is
exp: Productivity = 24000 / 48 = 500 LOC per person-month.

q: Changing the internal structure of code to improve its readability and maintainability without changing its external behaviour is called
exp: Refactoring restructures existing code while preserving its observable behaviour.

q: In basic COCOMO, the exponent b in E = a x (KLOC)^b for an embedded project is:
exp: Basic COCOMO constants: organic (2.4, 1.05), semi-detached (3.0, 1.12), embedded (3.6, 1.20). 0.38 is the organic time exponent d.

q: In PERT, an activity has optimistic time 2 days, most likely time 5 days and pessimistic time 14 days. The expected time is
The question 'Are we building the product right?' relates to
exp: Verification checks conformance to specification (building the product right); validation asks whether we are building the right product.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the five information-domain components counted in Function Point Analysis?
exp: FP counts external inputs, external outputs, external inquiries, internal logical files and external interface files. Number of classes is an object-oriented size measure.

q: In Scrum, who is primarily responsible for maximizing the value of the product and managing the product backlog?
exp: The Product Owner owns and prioritizes the product backlog.

q: Which document serves as the formal description of what a software system is to do, agreed between customer and developer?
exp: The SRS records the agreed functional and non-functional requirements of the system.

q: In UML, which diagram best shows the time-ordered sequence of messages exchanged between objects?
exp: A sequence diagram arranges object interactions along a vertical time axis.

q: Statement I: 100% branch coverage guarantees 100% statement coverage (for code without unreachable statements). Statement II: 100% statement coverage guarantees 100% branch coverage. Which is correct?
options: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
Statement I is false and Statement II is true
exp: Executing every branch executes every statement, but executing every statement may still miss e.g. the false outcome of an if without else.

q: Sandwich (hybrid) integration testing combines:
exp: Sandwich testing integrates the top layers top-down with stubs while the lower layers are integrated bottom-up with drivers, meeting in the middle.

q: Match: 1 Corrective, 2 Adaptive, 3 Perfective, 4 Preventive with a) fixing defects, b) adjusting to a new operating system, c) adding requested features, d) restructuring to avoid future problems. Select the correct matching.
exp: Corrective fixes faults, adaptive responds to environment change, perfective adds/enhances features, preventive restructures for future maintainability.

q: Which of the following is NOT a CASE tool?
options: A code generator from design models
A spreadsheet-based payroll application used by the accounts department
exp: CASE tools assist software development activities; a payroll application is an end-user application, not a development aid.

q: A Gantt chart is mainly used to show
options: Project tasks as bars against a time scale
The flow of data between processes
The degree of coupling among modules
exp: A Gantt chart plots task start, duration and finish as horizontal bars over a calendar.

q: In Six Sigma quality, the target defect level is approximately
exp: Six Sigma aims at no more than 3.4 defects per million opportunities.

q: In McCall's quality model, which of the following is a product transition factor?
exp: Product transition: portability, reusability, interoperability. Product operation: correctness, reliability, efficiency, integrity, usability. Product revision: maintainability, flexibility, testability.
